:::{#sol-log-partition-second-derivative}

The left side of @exr-log-partition-second-derivative differentiates to the second derivative of $\logpartitionf{\natparam}$.
On the right side,
the derivative moves inside the integral,
where only the density depends on $\natparam$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dif{}{\natparam} \int \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar
&= \int \statf{\rvar} \, \dif{\pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam}}{\natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the derivative of the integral is the integral of the derivative)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of the density follows from its form in @eq-exponential-family:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dif{\pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam}}{\natparam}
&= \dif{}{\natparam} \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}}
&& \text{(definition of an exponential family)}\\
&= \basemeasuref{\rvar} \, \expf{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}} \, \dif{\paren{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}}}{\natparam}
&& \text{(chain rule)}\\
&= \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, \dif{\paren{\natparam \, \statf{\rvar} - \logpartitionf{\natparam}}}{\natparam}
&& \text{(definition of an exponential family)}\\
&= \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, \paren{\statf{\rvar} - \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}}
&& \text{(the derivative of a difference is the difference of the derivatives)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this derivative into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int \statf{\rvar} \, \dif{\pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam}}{\natparam} \, d\rvar
&= \int \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, \paren{\statf{\rvar} - \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(substitute the derivative of the density)}\\
&= \int \paren{\sqf{\statf{\rvar}} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} - \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam} \, \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam}} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(distribute the product over the difference)}\\
&= \int \sqf{\statf{\rvar}} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar - \int \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam} \, \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(the integral of a difference is the difference of the integrals)}\\
&= \int \sqf{\statf{\rvar}} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar - \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam} \int \statf{\rvar} \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \natparam} \, d\rvar
&& \text{(a factor free of the integration variable moves out of the integral)}\\
&= \E{\sqf{\statf{\Rvar}}} - \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam} \, \E{\statf{\Rvar}}
&& \text{(definition of the expectation)}\\
&= \E{\sqf{\statf{\Rvar}}} - \sqf{\E{\statf{\Rvar}}}
&& \text{(the derivative of the log-partition function is the mean of the statistic)}\\
&= \Var{\statf{\Rvar}}
&& \text{(the second moment is the variance plus the squared mean)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The last line rearranges the second moment of $\statf{\Rvar}$,
which is its variance plus the square of its mean.
Equating the two sides of @exr-log-partition-second-derivative gives the result.

:::
